advances: All-dimensional containment on the boundary stratum of the auxiliary stochastic capacity problem.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For $d\ge2$, the final proof paragraph of fact c80576b633835713 gives capacity equal to the geometric mean of the other entries when a row has one zero and capacity zero with two or more zeros. For $d=1$, a row $(0,b)$ with $b>0$ has $F(t)=t/b$ on $0<t\le b$ and $F(t)=1$ above $b$, so its capacity is $b$. The all-zero row has capacity zero. Thus the same fixed-support formulas apply in all cases.

Fix $c\ge0$. Disregard rows of capacity zero. Group the other rows by their unique zero column. In each group choose a row label of maximal weight, replace that row by the sum of the group, and erase the other rows in the group. The new weighted geometric-mean contribution is at least the old weighted capacity contribution, by nonnegativity of the weights and geometric-mean superadditivity. The surviving labels have distinct zero columns, so some column permutation puts each of those zeros on its own row's diagonal. No column budget exceeds one, because merging preserved the column totals of the retained rows. Fill each remaining column budget by adding it to an off-diagonal row, possible since $d+1\ge2$. No off-diagonal row mean decreases. This gives a matrix admissible for $D_d$ with weighted mean objective at least $c\cdot(\phi_d(X_i))_i$.

The support inequalities for all $c\ge0$ imply membership in the compact convex downward set $D_d$, by the nonnegative-separation argument in the support-dual proof. The matrix used to establish each support inequality may depend on $c$.
statement: For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. For $d\ge1$ and $m=d+1$, let $D_d$ consist of all $v\in\mathbb R_+^m$ for which there exists a nonnegative zero-diagonal column-stochastic $m\times m$ matrix $Y$ satisfying $v_i\le \operatorname{GM}_d((Y_{ij})_{j\ne i})$ for every $i$, where $\operatorname{GM}_d$ is the geometric mean of $d$ entries. If $X$ is any nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrix with at least one zero entry in every row, then $(\phi_d(X_i))_i\in D_d$.
title: Stochastic capacity containment when each row has a zero
